verdicts.tldr: A free g1 address-namespace app becomes the front page's newest activity moment ('… just joined'), though New and Rediscover leave such apps out; the ADR specifies the feed this way, so this is a design tradeoff, not a defect.
verdicts.details: writeActivity filters only on e.Listing.shownApp() (api.gno:188), and track (pulse.gno:55) gates only on l.indexed(), so a confirmed g1 listing's 'listed' event is served and gnoweb's latestMoment (view.go:454) phrases it as 'Anon App just joined'. ADR-004 §Activity feed defines the ring as 'the last 20 events of confirmed, visible listings' and the Moments row as shown to 'everyone', with no namespace filter, so the code matches its spec. Only newApps' comment ('a free g1… namespace earns no front-page slot') reads otherwise. The moment is one line, pushed out by the next event, and each new key pays gas and deposit per deploy. Fix: if the store means to keep address namespaces off the front entirely, skip events whose listing has address(l.Namespace).IsValid() in writeActivity (or in latestMoment); otherwise reword newApps' comment to say 'no grid slot'.

List yours from a registered namespace: it opens here.","slugs":[]' and 'after deploy, activity: [{"kind":"listed","slug":"anon-app","stars":0},{"kind":"listed","slug":"valopers",...}]'. verdicts.tldr: Any g1 address-namespace app gets a front-page card in Recently updated by changing its tagline once a week, which undoes the namedApps exclusion that keeps those apps out of New and Rediscover.
verdicts.details: homeShelves calls listShelf(mustList("updated", h)) (front.gno:64), which windows apps.updated (shelves.gno:51). touch (listing.gno:244-255) writes every indexed listing into that index, whatever its namespace, while New and Rediscover read namedApps, filled only when !address(l.Namespace).IsValid() (listing.gno:301). A fresh key deploys gno.land/r/<g1addr>/app, waits updateCooldown, calls Register with a new tagline, and that app is the first card of Recently updated in api/v1/home and in the markdown front, while New stays empty and says 'List yours from a registered namespace'. The cooldown is per listing and keys are free, so a set of staggered g1 listings can keep the 8 cards gnoweb draws, which on a quiet chain is the whole shelf. ADR-004's Recently updated row sets no namespace rule, so the author may have meant it; the conflict is with newApps' comment ('its apps stay in :latest and their category') and the New row ('address (g1…) namespaces earn no front-page slot'). Fix: in homeShelves, filter the updated shelf's window the way namedApps does (skip listings whose address(l.Namespace).IsValid()), or keep a named-only updated index for the front and leave :updated whole.

Read front.gno:43-45,64; listing.gno:244-255,298-303; shelves.gno:51; ADR-004 rows New and Recently updated. The realm does not exist at the merge base.

verdicts.tldr: While GovDAO has r/sys/names paused, a namespace owner's star on their own app is stored as ranked and stays ranked after the pause ends, breaking 'stars on apps in your own namespace never rank'.
verdicts.details: Star computes ranked as named && mature && !ownsNamespace(caller, l.Namespace) (store.gno:170). When names is enabled, ownsNamespace returns names.IsAuthorizedAddressForNamespace (store.gno:117), and that goes through verifier, which returns false whenever isPaused (verifier.gno: 'if isPaused { return false // emergency halt: reject every deploy including PA }'). The store uses a deploy gate as its ownership check, so during a pause every owner looks like a stranger. The star is stored as Ranked=true and feeds Top, trending, builder totals and confirmation (1 of the 3 ranked stars) for the owner's own listing after unpause. The same branch makes Claim panic for the length of the pause. The gain is one ranked star per own app, only inside a GovDAO emergency window. Fix: decide ownership without the pause, e.g. compare addr.String() == ns for address namespaces and resolve the registered name's owner through r/sys/users, instead of calling the deploy verifier.
